Definition: from the base of G297 and ἕννυμι (to invest); to enrobe:--clothe.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus asks, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which today is and tomorrow is cast into the oven, shall He not much more clothe you? And when He speaks of John the Baptist, He asks what the crowds went out to see — a man clothed in soft raiment? The word is used for God clothing His creation and for men dressed in fine clothes, and the contrast is the point.
TheologicalSignificance: Two verses about clothing carry no doctrine of their own; their weight is Jesus' argument — if God dresses the grass, He will dress His people, and soft clothes belong in kings' courts, not in the wilderness where a prophet stands.
